headline: Deep depression forms in Bay, ports on alert
summary: A low-pressure system has intensified into a deep depression, prompting warning signal No. 3 for several major sea ports.
details: A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a deep depression, moving northwest toward the Indian coast.
At 9pm Tuesday, the system was located 875km southwest of Chattogram, 850km southwest of Cox’s Bazar, 695km southwest of Mongla, and 720km southwest of Payra.
Winds near the center are reaching 50kmph, with gusts up to 60kmph, creating rough seas in the north Bay.
Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been instructed to keep local warning signal No. 3 hoisted.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the north Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and operate with caution until further notice.
Meteorologist Khandaker Hafizur Rahman stated that while it is unlikely to develop into a cyclone for now, it may bring rain to the southern and southwestern parts of the country.

topic: smuggled bangladeshi fertiliser feeding myanmar conflict
headline_marked: Over 15,000kg of [[smuggled fertiliser bound for Myanmar]] seized
headline: Over 15,000kg of smuggled fertiliser bound for Myanmar seized
summary: While local farmers face severe shortages, huge quantities of urea are allegedly being smuggled across the Naf River, potentially to be used in bomb-making.
details: Over 15,000kg of urea and other fertilisers were seized by police in Ukhiya between June 27 and August 27, most of which were allegedly destined for Myanmar.
Local farmers in areas like Anjumanpara report severe shortages, with some saying their rice plants are turning yellow and growth is being stunted because they cannot obtain fertiliser.
Security officials and analysts warn that this trade may operate as a barter system, with drugs and weapons potentially flowing back into Bangladesh from across the border.
There are further allegations that the urea is being used to manufacture bombs in Myanmar's conflict zones, adding a dangerous dimension to the smuggling operation.
Smugglers reportedly use a network of Rohingya refugees and local carriers to move small consignments in plastic containers or sacks to avoid detection by the BGB.
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has conducted multiple seizures, including 100 sacks of urea in June and further detentions of Rohingya camp residents involved in the transport.
Ukhiya Upazila Agriculture Officer Kamanashish Sarkar noted that much of the seized fertiliser likely comes from outside the region, as the quantities exceed local official allocations.
Local representatives suggest that while vehicles leaving the area are searched, those entering are not, facilitating the movement of fertiliser into the border region for smuggling.
